messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redwood-inference-serving (inference-pool-01) — high 5xx rate detected. Severity: P2. Incident id: INC-2026-195555. Page sent to: @emma (primary oncall).

emma (oncall): Acking. jumping in now. reading logs.

pagerduty: ack received from emma at +1m

emma (oncall): quick check — CPU on pool-01 nodes normal, but host logs show repeated kv-cache OOMs. rolling restart of worker-1.

sara (engineer): tagging in — saw similar yesterday after a deploy; can we confirm recent rollout? @eng-runtime

emma (oncall): yup there's a canary from 01:12, build sha abc123. I'm running `kubectl describe rs inference-deploy-canary` and `kubectl logs -f worker-1`.

emma (oncall): logs snippet:
```
2026-03-14T01:17:22Z WARN kv_cache: reserve failed: out of memory
2026-03-14T01:17:22Z ERROR request: handler crashed: index 0
```
snippet shows OOMs spike aligned with 01:17

pagerduty: escalation timer: no further ack in 7m -> will escalate to secondary @ryan

emma (oncall): attempting restart on worker-1: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n prod --selector=pool=pool-01`

ryan (sre-secondary): got the escalation, on my way. deploying a quick patch to limit kv cache size to 2GB, will patch configmap then restart.

sara (engineer): any customer impact currently? telemetry shows latency spike, 503s at 01:17 — about 3% of traffic hitting affected pool.

emma (oncall): contacting SRE-runbook: rolling restart accepted. applying patch now.

pagerduty: auto-escalation: secondary ack required; if no ack in 5m, will escalate to manager @luis

ryan (sre-secondary): patch applied, scaling down worker replica to 2 then back to 4 to clear stuck caches.

emma (oncall): after restart error rate dropped but not to baseline — a portion of traffic still hitting degraded replicas in AZ-a. failing over routing to pool-02.

sara (engineer): please run `curl -X POST https://console.internal/routing/failover -d '{"from":"pool-01","to":"pool-02","percent":80}'` (use internal token).

emma (oncall): initiated failover 80% -> pool-02. monitoring.

pagerduty: escalation: manager escalation fired to @luis at +13m (no secondary ack within policy window)

luis (manager): I'm awake, joining. what's the current blast radius? any revenue impact?

emma (oncall): latency increased for ~3% of production requests, errors ~3-4% at peak. customer-visible errors were limited to low-rate LLM infers. No major revenue impact but SLOs degraded.

luis (manager): ok prioritize containment and postmortem. agree with failover. once stable we should revert canary and pin rollback.

ryan (sre-secondary): failover metrics look good. error rate now back to 0.6% and latency within SLO. continuing to watch for 10m.

sara (engineer): leaving a note in #incidents-runbook: possible regression from canary 2026-03-14T01:12

emma (oncall): ack handoff to @ryan for next 2h while I sleep. creating handoff message.

emma (oncall): handoff:
- status: degraded -> contained
- mitigation: patch kv-cache limit + restart + 80% failover to pool-02
- followups: rollback canary, add kv-cache guard, add alert for kv-cache OOM
- owner: ryan

ryan (sre-secondary): got it. I'll run full soak and trigger rollback candidate if any reoccurrence.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-195555 status updated: mitigated -> monitoring. paging suppressed.

ryan (sre-secondary): closing thread in 30m if stable. thanks all :thumbsup:
